attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He mentions Piekniewski as an influence but states the claim himself.

semantics.note: Keeps 'all the major' and each 'almost exactly'. It is a firm present-tense description, though rhetorical in tone. Treating it as an observation is acceptable.

contract.note: Reading it as substantially similar methods, interchangeable capabilities and shared weaknesses is fair and ordinary. Company membership, the April 1–20 window and the spending basis are evaluator choices; Marcus supplied none of them.

evidence.note: Meta's own disclosure of a standard decoder-only transformer. It backs the technology-similarity part for Meta only, not data, results or spending.

Mistral's own disclosure of a sparse MoE model with multilingual ability. MoE is a transformer variant, arguably a minor implementation difference under the contract, so it does not clearly defeat near-equivalence.
Google's own April disclosure of a 1M-token context and audio input. This is a partial capability difference against Llama 3's 8K text-only models, but it does not measure overall result quality.
GPT-4 report admitting hallucinations and reasoning errors. It covers one company before the window, with no cross-company failure comparison.
Mistral's CEO reports cash burn of about €25M over 12 months, given in August 2024. It casts doubt on 'billions' for every company, but the period, basis and currency don't match.

reviews.rationale: Only Meta's architecture evidence supports any part, and only for one company. Gemini's long context and audio, plus Mistral's MoE design, show some differences, but no matched evaluation shows they defeat near-equivalence. There is nothing on training-data overlap and no matched spending evidence for each company. The packet does not settle the claim either way.
